incidents.victim: Unnamed enterprise (Microsoft case study)
incidents.vector: Compromised an end-of-life F5 BIG-IP appliance, pivoted via SSH to a Linux host, exploited an unpatched internal Atlassian Confluence server for RCE, then used stolen service credentials to stage Kerberos relay attacks (CVE-2025-33073) against Active Directory.
incidents.impact: Full multi-domain intrusion crossing edge, Linux, SaaS and identity boundaries; threat actor obtained credentials from Confluence config files and conducted hands-on-keyboard reconnaissance and lateral movement toward domain controllers.

incidents.victim: European governmental organizations (Belgium, Italy, Serbia, Spain, Poland) and South African entities
incidents.vector: Open-source vulnerability scanning of internet-facing assets followed by deployment of custom backdoors that use Discord and Microsoft Graph (OneDrive) APIs for command-and-control, with SOCKS proxies and SoftEther VPN tunneling for stealth.
incidents.impact: Sustained cyberespionage access to multiple EU government networks; novel C2 over Discord/Microsoft Graph blends into legitimate cloud traffic, complicating detection and enabling long-dwell intelligence collection.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 customers (hundreds of organizations)
incidents.vector: AI-generated phishing lures impersonating Adobe, DocuSign and SharePoint trick users into completing Microsoft's legitimate OAuth device-code flow, granting attacker-controlled apps persistent tokens that bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: FBI public advisory on Kali365 platform (subscription $250/mo–$2,000/yr on Telegram); captured OAuth access and refresh tokens enable mailbox access, lateral phishing, BEC, fraud and data theft without ever stealing the user's password.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and technology firms in the U.S., Israel and the United Arab Emirates (plus two additional Middle Eastern entities)
incidents.vector: Tailored spear-phishing lures impersonating airlines, video-conferencing platforms and recruiters delivered ZIP archives that abused DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET application security and deploy six new RAT variants.
incidents.impact: Coordinated campaigns timed with the Middle East regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026; group demonstrated significant operational tempo and rapidly rotated Azure-hosted C2 infrastructure per target.

incidents.victim: DDoS targets including U.S. Department of Defense IP ranges and security researchers
incidents.vector: Kimwolf IoT botnet enslaved millions of internet-exposed devices (digital photo frames, web cameras) and rented attack capacity to other cybercriminals.
incidents.impact: Canadian authorities arrested 23-year-old Ottawa resident Jacob Butler ('Dort') after U.S. extradition warrant; DOJ says Kimwolf launched 25,000+ attack commands including a record-setting ~30 Tbps DDoS, with some victim losses exceeding $1M.

incidents.victim: GitHub (Microsoft)
incidents.vector: A Microsoft developer installed the malicious Nx Console VS Code extension that was poisoned during the TanStack 'Mini Shai-Hulud' supply chain attack a week earlier.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 internal GitHub code repositories exfiltrated and listed for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens. Grafana confirmed a separate compromise tied to the same TanStack incident.

incidents.victim: Telecommunications providers and ISPs in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, eastern Ukraine (Donbas) and other Central Asian markets
incidents.vector: 'Showboat' (a.k.a. kworker) Linux post-exploitation framework, shared between multiple Chinese threat clusters including Calypso, with LAN-scanning capabilities that infect devices not exposed to the public internet.
incidents.impact: Four-year covert intelligence collection campaign against small-market telcos that registered zero VirusTotal detections; PwC links activity to Calypso, which also uses Windows backdoor JFMBackdoor and PlugX.

incidents.victim: NYC Health + Hospitals
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: At least 1.8 million people affected; stolen data includes medical records and irreplaceable biometric data such as fingerprints and palm prints.

incidents.victim: BlueSky users and political discourse
incidents.vector: Account takeovers of legitimate BlueSky users via credential compromise.
incidents.impact: Hijacked accounts used since April 2026 to post pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda; BlueSky has been suspending accounts until owners can re-secure them.

incidents.victim: Wahlap arcade gaming customers (~19 million, primarily China)
incidents.vector: Unprotected Elasticsearch database exposed to the public internet for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Approximately 19 million customer records including WeChat-linked phone numbers and full names exposed; server now secured.

incidents.victim: Verus-Ethereum cross-chain bridge
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed (bridge exploit).
incidents.impact: Attackers stole approximately $11.58 million in crypto assets from the Verus-Ethereum bridge.

incidents.victim: Pierre & Vacances, Belambra, Gîtes de France
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Three French holiday booking sites breached; customer data being sold online by an individual operator known as ChimeraZ.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor created a public 'Private-CISA' GitHub repository, deliberately disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protection, and committed plaintext credentials, AWS GovCloud admin keys, and an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app with full code-read and CI/CD permissions.
incidents.impact: One of the most severe federal credential exposures in recent memory; repo existed since November 2025 and was still being remediated a week after disclosure. Senators Hassan and Thompson are demanding answers; risk that adversaries accessed the material before takedown.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia and the United Kingdom
incidents.vector: High-volume vishing impersonating internal IT/help-desk staff with passkey-migration pretext, paired with real-time adversary-in-the-middle credential and MFA capture; attacker then registers their own MFA device and uses Python/PowerShell scripts with stolen session cookies to bulk-exfiltrate from SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce and Zendesk via Microsoft Graph.
incidents.impact: GTIG details case in which a single Python script downloaded over a million files from one victim's SharePoint and OneDrive; group has escalated to spam floods, threatening voicemails to executives and even swatting when victims do not respond to ransom demands.

incidents.victim: RXNT (electronic prescribing platform) – including U.S. Members of Congress
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; original breach occurred in March 2026.
incidents.impact: Patient prescription data stolen; affected individuals include Members of Congress, who use RXNT for prescriptions. RXNT notified authorities on the final day allowed under U.S. health-privacy regulations.

incidents.victim: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller / Manager customers worldwide
incidents.attacker: Unknown — likely sophisticated actor (UAT-8616) plus multiple opportunistic clusters
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of authentication-bypass CVE-2026-20182 to gain admin access, plus chained exploitation of CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122 using publicly released proof-of-concept code, followed by deployment of XenShell, Godzilla, Behinder, AdaptixC2, Sliver and XMRig payloads.
incidents.impact: At least ten distinct post-compromise clusters observed since March; UAT-8616 infrastructure overlaps with known Operational Relay Box (ORB) networks. Defenders urged to patch immediately.

incidents.victim: npm and PyPI ecosystem (TanStack, Mistral AI, UiPath, OpenSearch, Intercom client, dozens of other publishers)
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored, financially motivated (TeamPCP, a.k.a. UNC6780)
incidents.vector: Chained three GitHub Actions weaknesses with no stolen credential required: malicious pull_request_target trigger in a fork, GitHub Actions cache poisoning, and OIDC token extraction from runner memory during release.yml execution — producing 84 signed package publishes within six minutes that propagated worm-style across the dependency graph.
incidents.impact: By end of day on May 11: 373 malicious versions across 169 npm packages plus compromised PyPI packages, affecting ~520 million cumulative weekly downloads. First documented case of malicious npm packages bearing valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance. Source code for the worm was published on May 12, spawning copycat campaigns.

incidents.victim: 7-Eleven
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Retail chain disclosed an April data breach to U.S. state authorities; ShinyHunters listed 7-Eleven on its dark-web leak site.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands (U.S. territory)
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; ransomware not confirmed.
incidents.impact: Cyberattack disrupted government email servers; officials expect administrative slowdowns until full restoration.

incidents.victim: Post Luxembourg (state-owned telecom operator)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an undisclosed zero-day vulnerability in Huawei enterprise routers.
incidents.impact: Caused extended internet outages in Luxembourg in July 2024; details of the underlying zero-day remain undisclosed by both the telco and Huawei nine months later.
